title: Relative finite locally free locus commutes with arbitrary base change
statement: Let $p:Y\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [pqf-def-coherent] of finite presentation, meaning locally the cokernel of a map $\mathcal O_Y^m\to\mathcal O_Y^n$ for finite $m,n$. Assume $F$ is flat over $T$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Define $W(F)\subseteq |Y|$ to consist of points with a Zariski open neighbourhood on which $F$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal O^{\oplus r}$ for some finite $r\geq0$ [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf]. Then $W(F)$ is open. For every scheme morphism $v:T_1\to T$, put $Y_1=Y\times_TT_1$ with projection $q:Y_1\to Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For the tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], one has $W(q^*F)=q^{-1}(W(F))$. No flatness or finite-presentation hypothesis is imposed on $v$, no flatness hypothesis is imposed on $p$, and no Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on the schemes.

source.place: Tag 0CZR, lemma-finite-free-open (scheme version of spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 0CZT, lemma-finite-free-open, used in quot.tex Tag 0D03).

proof.text: The set $W(F)$ is the union of the open neighbourhoods on which $F$ is finite free, hence is open. Put $V(F)=\{y:F_y\text{ is flat over }\mathcal O_{Y,y}\}$. We will identify this set with $W(F)$.

For $y\in W(F)$ its stalk is finite free, hence flat by [lem-sc-affine-standard-cover-finite-free-local-fp-flat]. Conversely, if $y\in V(F)$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-source-stalk] makes $F_y$ finitely presented, hence finitely generated. The ring $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is local, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free] makes $F_y$ free. A finitely generated free module has a finite basis: express a finite generating family in any basis; the finite union of its supports contains every basis vector. Apply [lem-trf-finite-presentation-stalk-basis-spread] to this basis and $F$ to obtain a finite free neighbourhood of $y$. Thus $V(F)=W(F)$, including the empty basis when $F_y=0$.

Apply [lem-sfb-relative-module-flat-locus-base-change] with $S=T$, $X=Z=Y$, $p=a$ the given morphism, $f=\mathrm{id}_Y$, and $\mathcal M=F$. The hypothesis that $a=p$ is locally of finite type is [lem-a1-map-over-base-finite-presentation] applied with $X=Y$, $Y=S=T$, $q=\mathrm{id}_T$ (locally of finite type, since the preimage of an affine $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is itself, finitely generated over $A$) and $h=p$. All remaining hypotheses are precisely those of the item; in particular the flat object is $F$, not $Y$. The base-changed identity is $\mathrm{id}_{Y_1}$, so for $G=q^*F$ the result is $\{z:G_z\text{ flat over }\mathcal O_{Y_1,z}\}=q^{-1}(V(F))$.

source.place: Tag 0CZR, lemma-finite-free-open, proof; morphisms.tex Tag 01TW, lemma-finite-presentation-finite-type, for the finite-type hypothesis.

proof.text: If $z\in W(G)$, its stalk is finite free and therefore flat by [lem-sc-affine-standard-cover-finite-free-local-fp-flat]. Step 3 and $V(F)=W(F)$ give $q(z)\in W(F)$. Conversely take $q(z)\in W(F)$, and choose $U\ni q(z)$ with $F|_U\cong\mathcal O_U^r$. The tensor definition [def-pc-module-pullback] gives $G|_{q^{-1}U}\cong\mathcal O_{q^{-1}U}^r$: the coordinate map $a\otimes(b_i)\mapsto(ab_i)$ has inverse $(c_i)\mapsto\sum_i c_i\otimes e_i$, compatibly with restrictions. Thus $z\in W(G)$. The two inclusions give the required equality for arbitrary $v$.
